calls.text: {"hypotheses":[{"cause":"Process invoking abort() due to heap or memory corruption","detail":"Exit code 134 maps to SIGABRT (128+6). In native runtimes this signal is raised by the allocator on double-free, heap metadata corruption, or explicit abort() calls — none of which trigger the OOM killer, consistent with oom_killed=✗. The crash recurs deterministically (BackOff count=12) suggesting a reproducible code path rather than a transient resource spike. Infrastructure angle: if the container memory limit is set too close to actual working set, the allocator may corrupt internal bookkeeping under pressure even when the node itself shows no resource_pressure.","anchored_facts":["process_crash","crashloop"],"confidence":0.72},{"cause":"Missing or incompatible shared library / dynamic linker abort at container startup","detail":"SIGABRT is sent by the dynamic linker (ld.so) when a required symbol or library is unresolvable at dlopen time on some libc versions, producing exit_code=134 with no application log. The fact that max_restart_count=0 in one observation (fresh pod) yet BackOff count=12 exists suggests the crash happens very early — before the app writes any logs — which is consistent with a linker-level abort. Root cause could be a base image layer mismatch or a volume-mounted library path that is missing or stale in this preprod environment.","anchored_facts":["process_crash","crashloop"],"confidence":0.55},{"cause":"Persistent crash-loop driven by a deterministic SIGABRT with no self-healing path","detail":"The combination of BackOff count=12 and exit_code=134 (SIGABRT) with no OOM, no scheduling failure, and no recent deploy signal points to a container that crashes on every start due to an internal abort, and Kubernetes backoff is the only active mitigation. From an infra standpoint the kubelet will keep restarting indefinitely with exponential backoff (up to 5 min). If the SIGABRT source is a corrupted writable layer or a bad emptyDir/ConfigMap mount, the fix requires pod eviction and a clean reschedule rather than waiting for the backoff window.","anchored_facts":["crashloop","process_crash"],"confidence":0.60}]}

{"refutations": ["The hypothesis asserts the crash is deterministic across many restarts, citing BackOff count=12 as evidence. However, the only fact supplying that count is a ✓ crashloop (conf=0.38, source=k8s_event) explicitly marked attribution=unverified with note='namespace-wide event; alert has no pod/service label to attribute it to the target workload' — the 12 BackOff events may belong to a different workload entirely. The authoritative ✓ crashloop (conf=0.80, source=k8s_terminated_state) records max_restart_count=0 and recent_backoff_events=1, consistent with a single crash, not a repeating deterministic failure loop. This undercuts the 'deterministic on every startup' claim that the hypothesis uses to narrow causation to a code-path bug."]}

{"refutations": ["The hypothesis explicitly anchors part of its reasoning on 'BackOff count=12 exists' to infer very-early crashes, but the observed fact_kind 'crashloop (conf=0.38)' carries attribution=unverified and notes it is a 'namespace-wide event; alert has no pod/service label to attribute it to the target workload' — meaning this BackOff count cannot be reliably tied to bot-service-56567b98-5jmct, invalidating that inference.", "The hypothesis proposes 'base image layer mismatch' as a concrete root-cause mechanism, which requires a recent change to the image or its layers; the fact_kind 'recent_deploy (conf=0.70)' is marked ✗ (NOT observed, reason=no_deploys_or_no_timestamp), directly contradicting the premise that a freshly-introduced image incompatibility triggered the linker abort."]}

{"refutations": ["crashloop (conf=0.80, source=k8s_pod_status) shows max_restart_count=0 and phrase_hits=0, directly contradicting the hypothesis claim of a *persistent* crash-loop that 'crashes on every start' — a deterministic abort repeating across restarts would produce a non-zero restart count.", "crashloop (conf=0.38, source=k8s_event) explicitly carries attribution=unverified and the note 'namespace-wide event; alert has no pod/service label to attribute it to the target workload' — the BackOff count=12 that the hypothesis uses as a primary anchor cannot be reliably tied to bot-service-56567b98-5jmct, undermining the core evidence for the exponential-backoff narrative."]}

{"refutations": ["The hypothesis explicitly uses 'BackOff count=12 at namespace event level' as supporting evidence for the container 'exiting quickly and consistently each restart cycle,' but the ✓ crashloop (conf=0.38) fact states attribution=unverified and 'namespace-wide event; alert has no pod/service label to attribute it to the target workload' — this count cannot be reliably attributed to bot-service, undermining that pillar of the hypothesis.", "The pod-level ✓ crashloop (conf=0.80) fact shows recent_backoff_events=1 (not 12) and max_restart_count=0, directly contradicting the hypothesis's portrayal of 12 consistent restart cycles; a single observed backoff event does not establish the repeated, stable crash pattern the hypothesis relies on to argue the abort is deterministic and reproducible."]}
